title: Repetitive Motion and Carpal Tunnel Syndrome
osha_standards: OSH Act Section 5(a)(1) General Duty Clause
summary: Carpal tunnel syndrome comes from a nerve in the wrist being pinched over and over, causing pain, weakness, and tingling that can become disabling. This talk covers tool choice, wrist position, and rest.
talking_points: Use tools designed for the job and for the task at hand.
Choose tools that keep your wrist straight and neutral, not bent forward or back, to lower the force you use.
Use two-handled tools with a spring return so the handle opens on its own, and a locking position when constant force is needed.
Wear gloves or anti-vibration wraps to improve grip and cut down shock from vibrating tools.
Rest your hands regularly, reduce repeated movements, and change your arm position often during a task.
site_hazards_to_check: Tools that force the wrist into a bent position
Vibrating tools used without anti-vibration gloves or wraps
Tasks with constant repeated hand motions and no rotation or breaks
Worn or wrong-sized tools that need extra grip force
Cold hands, which raise the risk from vibration
discussion_questions: Which tasks today involve the most repeated hand and wrist motion?
Can any of those tasks be rotated among the crew?
What tool or glove changes would keep your wrist in a neutral position?
